correctness.rationale: With unit facet normals, P_r is the intersection of all inward-translated supporting halfspaces; dist(v,P_r+rB)=max(0,dist(v,P_r)-r). Convexity of the distance function reduces maximal opening loss to vertices. For each vertex its incident facet constraints imply dist(v,P_r)>=r lambda_v; the minimizing feasible tangent displacement meets nonincident facets for all sufficiently small r, giving local equality. In plane lambda_v=csc(theta_v/2). The polygon angle sum yields min theta <=(n-2)pi/n and global E/r>=sec(pi/n)-1. For regular n-gons the exact homothetic erosion gives equality all 0<r<=Rin. Monotone inverse-cosecant gives all-angle stability; rhombus perturbation proves linear order cannot improve. Independent square/rhombus check E/r=sqrt(2)-1, and inspected supplied clipping/LP numerical code; finite geometry checks do not establish all polygons.
residual_risks: No uniform small-radius equality threshold across different polygons; unit Euclidean normals crucial. At inradius endpoint P_r can be a singleton.

evidence: Cappello Theorem 1.1 is a characterization of C^(1,alpha) convex bodies via approximate inner balls, not a sharp nonsmooth n-gon side-count minimax Hausdorff theorem.
